indication.text: Adjunct to diet and exercise to reduce LDL-C in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH)

citations.quote: LEROCHOL™ is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).

target_moa.text: PCSK9 inhibitor; a recombinant fusion protein that binds PCSK9, blocking PCSK9-LDLR interaction and preventing LDLR degradation, thereby increasing LDLR-mediated clearance of LDL-C and lowering LDL-C levels

citations.quote: Lerodalcibep-liga is a recombinant fusion protein that binds PCSK9 with picomolar affinity. PCSK9 binds to low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) on the surface of hepatocytes to promote LDLR degradation within the liver. By inhibiting the binding of PCSK9 to LDLR, lerodalcibep-liga increases the number of LDLRs available to clear LDL-C from the blood, thereby lowering LDL-C levels.

modality.text: Recombinant fusion protein (PCSK9-binding domain fused to human serum albumin); other

citations.quote: Lerodalcibep-liga is a recombinant fusion protein therapeutic agent comprised of a proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9)-binding domain and human serum albumin (HSA).

key_safety.text: Common adverse reactions (≥1%) were injection site reactions, nasopharyngitis, diarrhea, nausea, and peripheral edema. In the pooled hypercholesterolemia trials, injection site reactions occurred in 12% (LIB003) vs 5% (placebo) and nasopharyngitis 15% vs 14%. In the HeFH trial, injection site reactions occurred in 18% vs 3%.

summary.text: Standard-review BLA approved on the basis of substantial evidence from three double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials (004 in HeFH; 005 and 006 in ASCVD/high-risk) demonstrating ~50% or greater LDL-C reduction, a surrogate for cardiovascular risk reduction; approved as a traditional (not accelerated) approval with an advisory committee not convened.

citations.quote: Priority or standardStandard

Trial 004 in subjects with HeFH and Trials LIB003-005 (referred to as Trial 005) and -006 (referred to as Trial 006) in subjects with ASCVD or at increased risk for ASCVD events demonstrated LDL-C reduction of 50% or greater in subjects on background LDL-C lowering therapy.

As described in the Benefit/Risk Framework below (Section 2.1), we conclude that the reduction in LDL-C, a surrogate for the reduction in risk for cardiovascular (CV) events, observed with use of LIB003 outweighs the risks when LIB003 is used as recommended in the approved labeling.
An advisory committee meeting was not convened for this application.
